Adriana Rosario   IT Manager Milwaukee, WI • itmanager@gmail.com • +1 414-555-0182
PROFILE SUMMARY
IT Manager with 13 years of experience leading IT operations in Fortune-500 financial services across financial services, 
healthcare, and regulated enterprise IT, specializing in IT strategy, service delivery leadership, and budget ownership, 
currently leading 14 IT staff.
Solid technical and operational foundation across service management (ITIL 4, Agile-ITSM hybrid), collaboration 
(Microsoft 365), identity (Entra ID), ticketing (ServiceNow), and security and compliance (SOC 2 Type II), with strong 
fundamentals in service-management discipline, budget ownership, and business-partnership instincts.
Deep expertise in IT strategy and roadmap ownership, service delivery against SLAs, budget and vendor management, and 
security and compliance oversight, applying practices such as ITIL-aligned change management and executive business 
reviews to deliver reliable, secure, and business-aligned IT operations.
Engaged business partner working cross-functionally with Finance, Security, HR, and business-unit leadership in ITIL-
driven IT organizations, contributing to executive steering committees, quarterly business reviews, and audit readiness 
forums with a pragmatic, outcome-first mindset.
Service-oriented leader who fosters a culture of service ownership and written-decision rigor while owning a $5.4M annual 
IT budget and leading weekly IT leadership review sessions plus IT all-hands and career-development cycles.
TECHNICAL SKILLS
Frameworks & Methodologies: ITIL 4, ITSM, COBIT, ISO 20000, Agile-ITSM hybrid, change management, problem 
management, service request management
Collaboration & Identity: Microsoft 365 (Exchange, Teams, SharePoint, OneDrive), Google Workspace, Active 
Directory, Entra ID, Okta, SCIM, conditional access
Infrastructure & Cloud: Windows Server, Linux server administration oversight, VMware vSphere, Hyper-V, Azure, 
AWS, GCP , Intune for endpoints, Jamf for macOS
Service Management Tools: ServiceNow (ITSM, Change, Problem, CMDB), Jira Service Management, Freshservice, 
Zendesk, SLA design, KPI dashboards
Security & Compliance: SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, HIPAA, GDPR, NIST CSF, access reviews, patch management 
oversight, vendor risk assessments, audit readiness
Budget & Vendor Management: Capex/opex budgeting, forecasting, contract negotiation, MSP management, license 
management, RFP/RFI, cloud cost optimization, TCO modeling
Leadership & People 
Management:
Performance management, 1:1 cadence, career-development planning, hiring loops, IT org 
design, cross-functional partnership, executive communication
Project, BC & DR: PMP-aware program leadership, M&A IT integration, ERP/SaaS rollouts, BCDR planning, RTO/
RPO design, tabletop exercises, post-incident reviews
EDUCATION
University of Wisconsin-Madison   B.B.A. in Management Information 
Systems
Madison, WI • Sep 2009 - May 
2013
WORK EXPERIENCE
Northwestern Mutual   IT Manager Milwaukee, WI • Jul 2020 - Present
Lead IT operations for a Fortune-100 financial-services regional hub, managing 14 IT staff across 4 functions (helpdesk 
and end-user support, systems and network administration, and identity and collaboration platforms) for 4,500 internal 
users across the HQ campus plus 9 regional offices.
Authored a 3-year IT roadmap covering M365 modernization, an Entra ID migration from on-prem AD, and ServiceNow 
rollout, securing executive sponsorship and delivering 2 of 3 roadmap phases on time and on budget.
Run IT operations against ITIL 4 SLAs on ServiceNow, sustaining 96% P1 resolution within 4 hours across 28,000 tickets 
per year and maintaining 91% CSAT on quarterly service surveys.
Manage an annual IT budget of $5.4M across capex and opex, negotiating 3 MSP and licensing cycles that saved $720k/
year while expanding coverage for hybrid endpoints.
Partner with the CISO on access controls, patch cadence, endpoint security, and audit readiness for SOC 2 Type II and 
NAIC cybersecurity examinations, clearing 2 back-to-back audits with zero IT findings.
Sponsored 7 cross-functional IT projects including a regional office buildout, an ERP module rollout, and an M&A IT 
integration for a 200-person acquisition, delivering the integration cutover on schedule with zero P1 incidents.
Primary IT point of contact for 8 business units and the regional VP forum, running quarterly IT business reviews and 
standing leadership 1:1s, with the CFO signing off on all 3 IT budget cycles under my tenure.
Aurora Health Care   IT Manager Milwaukee, WI • Jul 2015 - Jun 2020
Owned business continuity and disaster recovery for the regional medical group, including a warm-standby DR site and a 4 
hours RTO / 1 hour RPO standard across clinical applications, with quarterly failover tests all passing.
Authored or updated 22 IT policies covering acceptable use, BYOD, access, change management, and incident response, 
adopted as the regional IT standard and referenced in 2 annual HIPAA audits.
Hired 11 IT staff across helpdesk, sysadmin, and network roles over 4 years, mentored 4 promotions to senior IT roles, and 
sustained 91% retention across the team.
Worked closely with Clinical Operations, Finance, HR, and Compliance teams across 14 clinic sites, authoring 28 SOPs and 
runbooks that shaped the regional operating baseline and onboarding 9 new-hire IT engineers.

Casey Nakamura   System Administrator Denver, CO • sysadmin@gmail.com • +1 3035-2222
PROFILE SUMMARY
System Administrator with 8 years of experience operating enterprise IT environments across aerospace engineering, 
telecommunications, and enterprise IT, specializing in Linux + Windows administration, virtualization, and enterprise 
security hardening.
Solid technical background across operating systems (RHEL, Windows Server), virtualization (VMware vSphere), 
automation (Ansible, PowerShell), monitoring (Datadog, Nagios), and languages (Bash, Python) with strong fundamentals 
in networking fundamentals, change management, and audit-grade documentation.
Deep expertise in enterprise-grade reliability, defense-in-depth security, configuration management, and zero-touch 
provisioning, leveraging methodologies such as change-management workflows and quarterly DR drills to drive stable, 
secure, and well-documented infrastructure.
Engaged collaborator working cross-functionally with Engineering, Security, and Help Desk teams in ITIL-aligned 
environments, contributing to change-advisory boards, audit prep, and post-incident retrospectives with a pragmatic, 
ownership-first mindset.
Emerging leader who shares technical excellence and fosters a culture of operational rigor and documentation discipline 
through PR reviews and runbooks, while leading IT -ops guild sessions and authoring widely adopted runbook and SOP 
templates.
TECHNICAL SKILLS
Operating Systems: RHEL, Ubuntu, CentOS, Debian, Windows Server 2019/2022
Virtualization & Containers: VMware vSphere, Hyper-V, Proxmox, KVM, Docker
Networking: Cisco IOS, VLAN, DNS, DHCP , VPN (IPSec, OpenVPN), pfSense, Palo Alto firewalls
Security & Compliance: CIS benchmarks, CrowdStrike EDR, Tenable, MFA, SOC 2, ISO 27001
Monitoring & Backup: Datadog, Nagios, Zabbix, SolarWinds, Veeam, Commvault
Automation & Config: Ansible, Puppet, Chef, PowerShell DSC, Terraform
Scripting Languages: Bash, PowerShell, Python, Perl
Storage & Identity: NetApp SAN, Dell EMC, NFS/SMB, Active Directory, Okta SSO, LDAP
EDUCATION
University of Colorado Boulder   B.S. in Information Technology Boulder, CO • Sep 2014 - May 2018
WORK EXPERIENCE
Lockheed Martin Space   Senior Systems Administrator Denver, CO • Sep 2021 - Present
Owned server and OS administration for the Space Systems engineering environment supporting 2,500+ engineers, 
leading day-to-day operation across Linux fleet maintenance, Windows Server administration, and VMware virtualization 
for 600+ servers in a hybrid on-prem + Azure environment.
Managed user, group, and access policies for 8,000+ accounts across Active Directory and Okta SSO, applying role-based 
access control with least-privilege provisioning and automated joiner/leaver workflows from HR feeds, reducing access-
related help-desk tickets by 48%.
Configured and maintained enterprise networking covering VLAN segmentation, DNS and DHCP , site-to-site VPNs, and 
firewall rule policies across 40+ Cisco switches at 3 office sites, holding 99.98% LAN uptime under change-managed 
maintenance windows.
Hardened the fleet through monthly OS patch cycles on CIS-benchmarked baselines, CrowdStrike EDR rollout, and 
vulnerability remediation via Tenable, closing 180+ critical CVEs and lifting compliance posture from 78% to 97% for SOC 2 
audit readiness.
Built centralized monitoring on Datadog and Nagios for 600+ servers and 150+ services, defining SLO-style alert 
thresholds with on-call rotation rules and an alert-fatigue review cadence, cutting mean time to detect from 24 minutes to 
2 minutes.
Administered enterprise storage and virtualization on NetApp SAN and VMware vSphere clusters, running 120TB of file 
shares and 180+ VMs with RAID-10 layouts, automated tiering, and vMotion migrations for zero-downtime maintenance.
Reduced operational toil from 38% to 14% through Ansible playbooks for OS provisioning and patching, PowerShell DSC for 
Windows configuration, and Python scripts for inventory and audit reporting, reclaiming 480+ engineer-hours per quarter 
for the team.
Charter Communications   Systems Administrator Englewood, CO • Jul 2018 - Aug 2021
Designed and operated the enterprise backup and disaster recovery program on Veeam-based image backups, Commvault 
for application data, and quarterly restore drills, lifting recovery point objective from 24h to 4h and successfully recovering 
all 5 inadvertent data-loss events without impact.
Led incident response across 42 SEV1/SEV2 outages during on-call rotations, running systematic root-cause analysis, 
documented postmortems, and owner assignment for follow-ups, cutting mean time to resolve from 3.5 hours to 42 
minutes within the first year.
Maintained the team's operational documentation library covering 180+ runbooks, network and topology diagrams in 
Lucidchart, asset inventories in Snipe-IT, and standard operating procedures, clearing 2 back-to-back SOC 2 audits with 
zero findings.
Worked closely with Engineering, Security, and Help Desk teams across 5 office locations to coordinate change-
management windows, patch cycles, and infrastructure projects, authoring 9 operational SOPs that shaped the org's IT-ops 
standard and onboarding 6 new sysadmins.

Infrastructure Administrator  
 
 
 
 
COMPANY : SASFIN BANK LTD  
DIVISION : Information Technology 
JOB TITLE : Infrastructure Administrator 
MANAGER : Infrastructure Manager 
LOCATION :  Waverley, Johannesburg 
 
MAIN PURPOSE OF THE JOB 
 
The Infrastructure Administrator is responsible for ensuring that the performance and availability of the server and 
network infrastructure is maintained to the highest standard with maximum levels of productivity and efficiency. They are 
responsible for ongoing administration and support of all Infrastructure systems. 
 
Administrators are responsible for  
•  advising systematic know how of procedures, operat ions and work instructions 
•  checking systems and equipment for substandard per formance or malfunctioning 
•  fixing systems and equipment problems 
•  identifying performance problems and malfunctions 
•  maintaining hardware and corresponding documentati on of fixes, notes and recommendations 
•  performing hardware checks using appropriate testi ng and benchmarking tools 
•  daily infrastructure checks and reports 
 
Infrastructure deals with 
•  Communications and connectivity  :- , Network configuration, Network devices and equipment, Network 
infrastructure preparation, Network management tools, Network monitoring ( traffic, transmission quality, etc...), 
Network security, encryption and PKI, Network support, Phone, satellite, wireless and cables, Switch 
technologies and PBX’s, Telecommunications policy and standards, Backup and restore techniques, Logistics 
setup and maintenance,  Performance monitoring and tools, Service level agreements, Systematic and routine 
tasks, Updating live systems 
•  Enterprise security design :- Firewalls (hardware/software), Information security, Internet security, Securing 
different networks and connectivity types, Security for applications, databases and websites, Security for 
control and accessibility equipment, Security infrastructure, Security standards and protocols, Security tools, 
Server security, Security auditing 
 
An Infrastructure Administrator must have the ability to work on: 
•  Communications and connectivity 
•  Internet technologies, IP technologies 
•  Network devices and equipment 
•  Network management tools 
•  Networking design and diagrams 
•  Networking standards and protocols 
•  Routers, switches, hubs, and firewalls 
•  Wired, wireless, and satellite networks 
•  Windows Server Operating systems 
•  Systems Centre Products 
•  Microsoft Exchange 
•  Hyper V Hosts 
•  SAN Storage 
•  SQL Administration and monitoring 
 
KEY AREAS OF RESPONSIBILITY 
 
1. Monitoring 
a. Maintain monitoring and management platforms  
b. Monitoring network usage;  gathering monitoring statistics 
c. Managing routine preventative procedures and mai ntaining and monitoring network security 
d. Proactively manage the monitoring and reporting o f infrastructure capacity including bandwidth, 
storage etc. 
e. Provide capacity usage information to facilitate capacity planning 
 
 
 
 
2. Analysis 
a. Analysing and resolving faults,  
b. Ensuring that all IT equipment complies with indu stry standards;  
c. Monitoring network environments. 
d. Updating process, procedure. 
 
3. Installation and configuration (Maintenance and New Requirements) 
a. Administering  IT developments and undertaking pr oject work, 
b. Proactively maintain infrastructure to prevent fa ilures  
c. Maintenance of development and testing network e nvironments 
d. Supporting and maintaining new server hardware an d software infrastructure;  
e. Setting up of user accounts, permissions and pass words to ensure compliance with policy 
 
4. Technical Support 
a. Provide infrastructure tier 1 support 
b. Escalate to infrastructure tier 2 support (Infras tructure Engineers) or 3 rd  party when required 
c. Providing training and technical support for Infr astructure Administrators 
 
5. Operations 
a. Compile daily operational reporting for review b y management team 
b. Provide operational backup to other Infrastructur e Administrator in their absence 
 
DESCRIPTION OF TASKS 
 
1. Service Management 
a. Administer and support server and network infrast ructure 
b. Log and follow-up issues with Vendors 
c. Monitor and analyse system trends in the operati onal environment 
d. Perform health system checks on areas of responsi bility 
 
2. IT Procedures 
a. Ensure systems adhere to OLAs and SLAs 
b. Ensure projects, tasks and operations follow comp any and departmental policies and procedures 
 
3. Feedback and activity updates to: 
a. Line Manager : this role reports to Infrastructu re Manager 
b. Team Lead : this role feeds back to Infrastructu re Team Lead 
c. Service Manager : this role provides daily operat ional reporting to the Service Manager 
d. Infrastructure Engineers – this role is required  to do shift handover to other engineers. 
SKILLS AND QUALIFICATIONS REQUIRED 
 
1. Business / Industry Experience 
a. Experienced in banking, stockbroking, transactio nal finance, 
  
2. Education 
a. Matric plus an appropriate tertiary qualificatio n (NQF5 or above) with 1 years relevant experience in 
Infrastructure OR Matric with 2 years relevant experience in Infrastructure  
b. Microsoft Certified IT Professional (MCITP): Enterp rise Administrator 
c. HP Accredited Systems Engineer (ASE) 
d. Cisco Certified Network Associate (CCNA) 
e. Cisco Certified Network Associate: Voice (CCNA: Voi ce) 
 
3. Experience 
a. Minimum 2 years’ experience in maintaining Micro soft network in a medium to large scale environment 
b. Experience in a high-availability, online transa cting environment. 
c. Thorough understanding of Microsoft Windows Serve r System technologies 
 
4. Technology 
a. Experience managing Cisco network devices. 
b. Experience with Hewlett Packard server and storag e technologies. 
 
 
c. Experience with multiple storage and backup subs ystems. 
d. Experience with Cisco IP Telephony. 
 
5. Methodology 
a. Exposure to Microsoft Operations Framework (MOF)  with preference to attendance of course 1737 - MOF 
Essentials 
b. ITIL Foundations Certificate 
 
PERSONAL ATTRIBUTES 
 
•  Working  Style 
o Teamwork and cross collaboration ability 
o Mind-set that understands the critical importance of service availability, recoverability, maintainability and 
scalability. 
o Prepared to meet measurable targets for uptime and performance 
o Prepared to work after hours, shifts and be on stan dby on a scheduled basis. 
 
•  Communication skills 
o Ability to conduct technical planning sessions 
o Ability to feedback on technical issues in a struct ured manner 
 
•  Time Management 
o Solid work ethic with attention to detail 
o Ability to work under pressure 
 
•  Conformance 
o Strong process background in change control, backup  strategies and disaster recovery 
o Ability to adhere to very strict policies and proce dures 
o Focus on planning, testing and carefully controlle d implementations 
 
   REMUNERATION 
 
Total Cost to Company, market related depending on qualification and experience. 
Interested applicants can forward their CV to sasfinrecruitment@sasfin.com  by no later than: 12 July 2016.  
*Please consider your application unsuccessful if you have not received a response within 2 weeks of submission.

PROFILE SUMMARY
Senior Database Administrator with 8 years of experience operating enterprise SaaS and developer-tooling teams across 
ticketing, CI/CD, and observability platforms, specializing in high availability, disaster recovery, performance tuning, and 
zero-downtime change management.
Well-rounded skill set across relational (PostgreSQL, Oracle), NoSQL (MongoDB), managed cloud (AWS RDS), high 
availability (Patroni), backup (pgBackRest), schema migrations (Liquibase), and automation (Terraform, Ansible, Python).
Deep expertise in HA architecture, backup & DR, performance tuning, and change management, leveraging methodologies 
such as GitOps for DB and compliance audits to drive fast, reliable, and audit-ready database operations across the estate.
Engaged collaborator working cross-functionally with Platform, SRE, Security, Compliance, and Application teams in 
regulated SaaS environments, contributing to schema reviews, incident triage, and audit prep with a stability-first mindset.
Emerging leader who shares technical excellence and fosters a culture of zero-downtime migrations and 99.99% 
availability through schema-review office hours and DR drills, while leading DBA guild sessions and authoring widely 
adopted runbook and replication-pattern guides.
TECHNICAL SKILLS
Relational Databases: PostgreSQL, Oracle, SQL Server, MySQL, MariaDB, IBM Db2
NoSQL & In-Memory: MongoDB, Cassandra, DynamoDB, Redis, Elasticsearch
HA, Replication & Backup: Patroni, pgBackRest, Oracle Data Guard, RMAN, Always On AGs, MongoDB replica sets
Cloud & Managed Services: AWS RDS, AWS Aurora, Cloud SQL, Azure SQL, RDS Proxy, AWS Backup
Performance & Tuning: pg_stat_statements, AWR/ASH, SQL Profiler, Performance Insights, EXPLAIN ANALYZE, 
index tuning
Security & Compliance: TDE, TLS in transit, Kerberos, LDAP , AAD, row-level security, SOX, HIPAA, PCI, GDPR
Automation & IaC: Terraform, Ansible, Python, Bash, PowerShell, Liquibase, Flyway, GitHub Actions
Monitoring & Observability: Datadog, Prometheus + Grafana, CloudWatch, pgwatch2, Sentry, New Relic
EDUCATION
Boston University   B.S. in Computer Science Boston, MA • Sep 2014, May 2018
WORK EXPERIENCE
Atlassian   Senior Database Administrator Boston, MA • Aug 2022, Present
Led installation, configuration, and upgrades across multi-region AWS RDS and self-managed estates, standardizing patch 
and parameter workflows behind Datadog dashboards, and shipped 3 major-version upgrades across 18 clusters with 
rolling cutovers, blue-green swaps, and zero data loss.
Owned backup, recovery, and DR for 42 databases using pgBackRest with point-in-time recovery, ran weekly restore drills 
end-to-end across two geo-redundant regions, and held RPO ≤ 5 min and RTO ≤ 30 min across every quarterly DR test.
Stood up streaming replication and automated failover with Patroni across 18 production clusters, tuned witness quorum 
and connection routing through HAProxy, drove median failover to under 30 seconds, and lifted database availability from 
99.9% to 99.99%.
Owned performance monitoring and tuning using pg_stat_statements and execution-plan analysis, reindexed hot tables, 
partitioned the orders surface, cut p95 query latency from 840 ms to 120 ms, and sustained 12k QPS peak through Black 
Friday traffic.
Led security, access control, and compliance work: rolled out encryption at rest with AWS KMS, automated secrets rotation 
through HashiCorp Vault, layered row-level security, ran SOX and PCI audits with read-only auditor roles, and closed 47 
findings across 3 audit cycles.
Partnered with platform teams on schema change and release management via Liquibase, gated DDL through twice-
weekly review boards, change windows with rehearsed rollback playbooks, and read-only auditor sign-off, shipping 220 
migrations with 0 production outages.
Drove automation and Infrastructure as Code for provisioning and routine ops using Terraform and Ansible, replaced ticket-
based work with 14 self-service runbooks wired into GitHub Actions, and cut on-call toil by 60% in two quarters.
Akamai   Database Administrator Cambridge, MA • Jul 2018, Jul 2022
Managed Oracle Data Guard standbys for the legacy core, automating switchover and recovery with RMAN and custom 
Python tooling, cutting failover drill time from 4 hours to 35 minutes.
Owned capacity planning and storage for a 40 TB estate, partitioning hot tables, archiving cold data to S3, and reclaiming 9 
TB of storage while keeping read latency flat.
Established change management discipline with peer reviews on every DDL and a staging-before-prod gate, holding 
production-deploy success rate at 99.5% across 180 releases.
Mentored 2 junior DBAs, authored 6 runbooks (failover, RMAN restore, deadlock triage, replication health, capacity review, 
audit prep), and ran the on-call rotation for 15 production schemas.

Resume Reminders  
 
1. Appearances count!  Pay attention to how your resume looks.  Are there spelling errors?  Is space 
utilized efficiently and neatly?  As you proofread your resume, do you find yourself “skipping over” 
certain lines?  If so, perhaps they are too wordy.  Have 2-3 people proofread your resume to make sure 
all errors are caught. 
2. Size of Font.  Use 10-, 11- or 12-point font on your resume.  Headings can be printed in larger fonts to 
draw the reader’s attention, but avoid anything too large as it may look unprofessional. 
3. One page!  Unless you have over 10 years of relevant experience, your resume should be one page. If 
you go to 2 pages, put your name and “page 2” at the top of the second page. 
4. Truth or consequences.  Do NOT put untrue statements on your resume.  It can be grounds for 
termination! 
5. State your ACCOMPLISHMENTS not just your job description!  Don’t just copy your job duties 
straight from the job description.  Think about all of the things that make you an exceptional employee. 
Employers need to be able to see your results. 
6. Quantify your accomplishments.  Use number as indicators of how much you accomplished, 
whenever possible (example:  increased sales by 15%). 
7. No excuses.  Don't include reasons for leaving on your resume.  Save that for applications and 
interviews.  In the same manner, don’t point out your negatives, like a low GPA. 
8. Target your resume.  Think of your resume as an advertisement, and consider your career goal or 
objective when writing your resume.  Do the accomplishments, skills, etc. somehow reflect your career 
objective?   Use the language of your desired profession. 
9. Don’t include personal information.  Personal information about your marital status, religious 
affiliation, hobbies, family, age, or race does NOT belong on your resume. 
10. Know your audience.  Use the vocabulary of the hiring and/or department manager.  What skill sets 
that you have are they looking to hire?  In technical fields, what are the “keywords/skills” that employers 
are looking for?  Show how you would add value. 
11. Don’t include your salary history.   Save that for the interview process. 
12. Do not include the following statement on your resume, “References available upon request”. It 
is understood that you will provide references if so requested, and you are only wasting valuable space 
on your resume.  
13. Have references listed on a separate sheet and DO NOT include the list with your resume – you 
will be asked for them, so be prepared to supply the list when asked. Use professional references, such 
as previous employers/ supervisors, co-workers, and professors/ instructors. 
14. Use bold, italics, underlining and capitalization to highlight.  With the exception of scannable 
resumes, use these tricks to capture the reader’s attention to important parts of your resume.  However, 
make certain that the finished result is crisp & professional. 
15. Be neat!  Don’t fold, crease, or crumple your resume.  Your resume should be a demonstration of your 
very best work. 
16. Spell-check your resume over and over.  While you’re at it, check your phone number! 
17. Highlight your strengths by putting the most impressive sections of your resume FIRST.  If you have 
different sections that are equally impressive, use the most recent towards the top. 
18. Do NOT use pronouns.  Avoid complete sentences (this is one time when proper sentence structure is 
not used).  Your sentence structure in accomplishment statements should start with an action verb (see 
p.20) followed by an action statement.  Never use “I”. 
19. If you have multiple college degrees, begin with the highest degree first.  If you have two degrees at 
the same level (e.g. Bachelor’s degrees), start with the most recent. 
20. Don’t include a photograph of yourself when sending your resume. 
21. Use specific headings.  Instead of “Work History”, try using “Business Experience”. 
22. Resume paper required.  First impressions count, so choose your resume paper wisely.  The nicest 
paper will have cotton added, and will be in a professional color.  Your best bet is something light (white, 
beige, or gray).  Avoid splashy colors and overly feminine shades like pink.  Don’t use colored ink…plain 
black is best.  Also, remember that your resume may be photocopied, so avoid any kind of paper with a 
“grainy” look that may not photocopy well.

Creating an Electronic Resume 
 
When would you need an electronic resume? 
  Sending resumes via e-mail 
 Completing online job applications 
 Posting your resume to an online job board 
 
How is an electronic resume different from a traditional “paper” resume? 
More than likely, companies will feed your resume into a database.  Recruiters will search the 
databases using keywords to find the top candidates.  Thus, ensure that your resume is RICH 
with keywords for your field.  To determine keywords that might be used, look at a variety of job 
announcements to see what kinds of “buzz words” are being used.  Also, make sure that you list 
SPECIFIC names of programs & languages that you use.  Furthermore, the “appearance” of your 
electronic resume won’t matter as much since you will not be able to use bolding or large fonts. 
 
How do I transform my traditional resume into an electronic version?  
  In your word processing program, open the traditional resume. 
 Set the margins so that 6.5” of text is displayed. Enter 1” for the left margin and 1.75” 
for the right margin. With 6.5” margins, your finished document should fit into most 
email browsers and online application forms. 
 There are two ways to convert your traditional resume into an electronic 
version: 
a. One - Select all of the text and change the font to Courier, 12 point.  Using this font 
ensures that all of the letters are the same size.  Copy the document and paste it 
into Notepad, Wordpad or some other text editor.  Now you are ready to make 
additional changes. 
b. The other - Start Microsoft Word. Open your .doc resume file. Save your .doc resume 
file as a Text Only (*.txt) file. You'll note that your resume hasn't changed. Close 
the .txt file. To see the changes, open the .txt file. Now you are ready to reformat 
your resume and save it. 
 Replace all bullets and characters.  For bullets, you can use an asterisk or hyphen.  For 
characters such as $ or %, just write out the words “dollars” and “percent”. 
 To emphasize your name and section headings, use all CAPS. 
  Save the document when you have finished editing it in its entirety.   
 Cut and paste the document into a test email message.  You will paste the document 
directly into the body of the email.  Send the email to yourself and someone else to see 
how it looks to the recipient. 
 Finally, review what you have written.  Does it focus on skills, or duties?  Remember, if  
     your resume ends up in a recruiter’s database, you will need plenty of “keywords” in      
     it to ensure your resume is pulled up during their queries! 
 
Should I include a cover letter with my emailed resume? 
 Always include a cover letter when you are sending a resume through the U.S. mail or 
electronic mail. 
 In the body of the email, write the cover letter first.  After the signature line, put a line 
reading “RESUME FOLLOWS”.  Then, cut and paste your electronic resume after the 
cover letter
